sources.citation: Robert B. Zajonc (1968). Attitudinal effects of mere exposure. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1968) in Journal of Personality and Social Psychology establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: Richard L. Moreland, Robert B. Zajonc (1979). Exposure effects may not depend on stimulus recognition. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
sources.notes: Moreland & Zajonc (1979) JPSP proving exposure-driven liking operates independently of conscious stimulus recognition.

sources.citation: S. Jay Samuels (1970). Recognition of Flashed Words by Children. Child Development.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (1970) in Child Development extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Eugene Burnstein (2009). Robert B. Zajonc (1923–2008). American Psychologist.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2009) in American Psychologist extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Robert F. Bornstein (1989). Exposure and affect: Overview and meta-analysis of research, 1968–1987. Psychological Bulletin.
sources.notes: Robert Bornstein's 208-study meta-analysis establishing robustness, ceiling saturation, and subliminal amplification of Zajonc's mere exposure effect.

Huang Tingjian originally composed the seven-character poem "Besotted by Flower Vapors" in 1087. It is one of two poems that Huang Tingjian mailed to his friend Wang Gong (王鞏)—who had solicitously gifted flower.
